candidates.original_title: Sociodemographic aspects and health care-related outcomes: a latent class analysis of informal dementia care dyads
candidates.description: Latent class analysis identifying six subgroups of informal dementia care dyads based on sociodemographic characteristics in a German sample of 551 dyads
candidates.citation_sentence: The present study is designed as a replication of a previous LCA, which was carried out with baseline data of the German DemNet-D study [22].
candidates.notes: The authors explicitly state that 'the findings of the present study confirm those of the original LCA.' The replication uses the same LCA methodology (Step-3 approach, same indicator variables as much as possible) but with a Dutch sample (COMPAS) instead of the German original (DemNet-D), making it a close extension. No traditional effect sizes or p-values are reported for the LCA results in either the original or replication.

candidates.original_title: Sociodemographic aspects and health care-related outcomes: a latent class analysis of informal dementia care dyads
candidates.description: The original study claimed that six latent classes of community-dwelling informal dementia care dyads could be identified and that these dyad subgroups differed in health care-related outcomes.
candidates.citation_sentence: The present study is designed as a replication of a previous LCA, which was carried out with baseline data of the German DemNet-D study [22].
candidates.notes: The paper uses numbered citations rather than author-year citations; reference [22] identifies the original study and its DOI. The replication applies the same LCA approach to a structurally similar Dutch sample, so it is a close extension. Authors explicitly state that the findings confirm those of the original LCA.
